https://www.thetablet.co.uk/news/vatican.text: Vatican affirms support for Ukraine with high-profile visits Patrick Hudson 19 July 2026, The Tablet Prev Next Archbishop Gallagher during a visit to the Ukrainian Catholic University in Lviv on 17 July UGCC Department of Information Archbishop Paul Gallagher’s six-day visit is his second to Ukraine, following his first shortly after the full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022, while Cardinal Matteo Zuppi also visited the Lviv region and Kyiv last week. Pope Leo prayed for “countries torn apart by war and violence” after Vatican delegates visited Ukraine this week. “Let us not forget those who are suffering and dying because of these conflicts, and let us add our constant prayers to the generous efforts for peace ,” the Pope said on Sunday, speaking after the Angelus in the main square of Castel Gandolfo, outside Rome. The previous day, the Holy See’s secretary for relations with states Archbishop Paul Gallagher had visited bomb sites in Kyiv. Earlier in the week, the Archbishop of Bologna Cardinal Matteo Zuppi had made a four-day visit to Ukraine in his role as papal peace envoy. Archbishop Gallagher met parishioners at St Nicholas Church in Kyiv, which suffered a Russian missile strike in December 2024 that shattered its windows and caused severe damage to the interior. He said the community demonstrates “the virtue of perseverance”. “Perseverance is also a defining characteristic of our Catholic community. You have remained steadfast as a Eucharistic and prayerful community, and I can already see the fruits of that perseverance,” he said, emphasising Pope Leo’s support for them. “There is not a single day when he does not pray for Ukraine and for you, men and women of faith,” the archbishop continued. He voiced hope that the Pope would visit Kyiv “one day”. Gallagher later met members of the local authorities and emergency services at an apartment block destroyed by a Russian strike on 14 May which killed 24 people, including three children. Officials said that since June this year strikes have killed at least 300 people across Ukraine and injured thousands more. The archbishop also visited the St Thomas Aquinas Dominican Institute of Theology , which suffered shrapnel damage from nearby drone and missile strikes in May, and the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, the ancient monastery complex struck in a Russian attack last month . The visit officially marks 35 years since the restoration of the structures of the Latin-rite Church in Ukraine shortly before the collapse of the Soviet Union, and 25 years since the apostolic visit of John Paul II. Archbishop Gallagher arrived in the country on Thursday, travelling by road from Poland, and was received at the Krakovets border crossing by members of Ukraine’s foreign ministry. At a meeting the next day with local authorities at the curia of the Archdiocese of Lviv – the largest Roman Catholic diocese in Ukraine – Gallagher said the Church and the Pope “have not forgotten the suffering of the Ukrainian people and their sacrifices”. “A just end to the war means restoring peace to this part of Europe,” he said. “We must create the right conditions for a just peace .” On Sunday, the archbishop celebrated Mass at the National Shrine of Our Lady of the Holy Scapular in Berdychiv, alongside members of the Latin-rite hierarchy and the head of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church Major Archbishop Sviatoslav Shevchuk. “We ask the Lord God to truly heed the prayer of the Universal Catholic Church and put an end to this unjust war,” said Shevchuk in an address after the Mass. “We know that Vatican diplomacy is God’s work , because the Holy See, in particular Pope Leo XIV, is today a great herald of authentic peace.” The six-day visit is Gallagher’s second to Ukraine, following his first shortly after the full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022. Earlier this week, Cardinal Zuppi also visited the Lviv region and Kyiv. He previously travelled to the country in June 2023, when Pope Francis appointed him as his peace envoy, and has since worked to facilitate prisoner exchanges . After his arrival on Monday, Zuppi met prisoners of war held in the Zakhid-1 detention centre near Lviv and told them Pope Leo “is praying for you, that the war may end and that you may return home”. The prisoners, captured by Ukrainian forces while fighting with the Russian army, come from more than 50 countries. The cardinal distributed gifts sent by Pope Leo to the prisoners, including prayer cards and keychains. “The Pope asked me to bring you a keychain. I hope that soon you’ll put your house key on it,” he said. “We want to tell you today to look to the future with hope – that you will return home, that the war will end. And we pray fervently that it will end soon.” On Wednesday, Cardinal Zuppi offered a prayer during a ceremony in Kyiv for Ukrainian Statehood Day, marked on the same day as the commemoration of the Baptism of Kyivan Rus’ by Prince Volodymyr the Great in 988. “Grant a just peace. May prisoners return home, may children embrace their families once again, may the missing be found, and may everyone be able to mourn over the body of their loved one who has fallen. Inspire in each one of us the courage and wisdom to become builders of peace,” Zuppi said. During the ceremony in St Michael’s Square, the cardinal took part in a wreath-laying ceremony alongside President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, placing a bouquet of red roses before the Wall of Remembrance commemorating those killed in the war with Russia. Ukraine’s Ambassador to the Holy See Andrii Yurash called this an “exceptional gesture of respect toward Ukraine, acknowledging its statehood tradition, which dates back more than 1,000 years, as well as its ongoing struggle for independence in the war against the Russian aggressor”. Later that day, Zuppi met Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha for further discussion of prisoner exchanges and the repatriation of detained civilians and children. According to Vatican News, Ukrainian officials also requested the Holy See’s support for an “all-for-all” exchange involving around 7,000 Ukrainian prisoners held in Russia and roughly 4,000 Russian prisoners in Ukraine. “Even one soldier, one civilian or one child reunited with their family is a step towards peace,” Zuppi said. “Every possible effort will be made. This is the will of Leo XIV. Humanitarian commitment must stand above political or military considerations.” Archbishop gives Pope Leo list of Ukrainian prisoners Joy amid sorrow: two weeks in Ukraine Stay updated — add us as a preferred news source on Google: Archbishop Paul Gallagher Cardinal Matteo Zuppi CATHOLIC NEWS peace Pope Leo XIV prisoners of war Russia Russian invasion of Ukraine Ukraine Vatican diplomacy Help us keep The Tablet’s voice independent, clear and far-reaching. https://www.politico.eu/sponsored-conten.text: At this month’s NATO summit in Ankara, allies announced billions of dollars in new arms deals and reaffirmed their commitment to spend more on defense. European governments have made the pledge, and the money is real: European defense spending has doubled since 2019, and by 2030, European NATO member countries are projected to spend in excess of €800 billion a year, up €300 billion from 2025, with equipment spending alone nearly doubling. But committing money is the easy part. The harder question is whether Europe’s defense industry can turn it into equipment fast enough to matter. Europe’s largest defense manufacturers’ order books now average more than five years for production, and some are closer to nine. Money is flowing in faster than industry can turn it into equipment. But a purchase order is not equipment that can be deployed on the ground and the air. European countries have long duplicated capabilities rather than pooling them. The bottleneck sits in the defense industrial system. Deterrence relies on the chain from funding to contracts, then through production, deployment into services, then rapid innovation in the field. Europe’s next goal comes after the spending promise. The continent fields six times as many weapons platforms as the United States, because countries have long duplicated capabilities rather than pooling them. Production ends up split across many small runs that never reach an efficient scale. Ukraine, under pressure, has shown how fast a defense system can move, adapting tactics in weeks and building drone detection networks from consumer electronics. Europe needs to catch up and then accelerate. Advertisement Four moves would help Europe accelerate. The first is multi-speed procurement. Software-led systems such as drones and targeting improve in rapid cycles throughout their deployment and need procurement that can keep up. Israel’s Iron Dome started out as far less capable than it is today and improved continuously in service. European defense ministries have already set up high-speed procurement units with dedicated teams and greater risk tolerance. These need to become mainstream, rather than the exception. Collaboration in procurement, maintenance and training brings costs down and delivery forward. The second is military collaboration to reduce fragmentation. Collaboration in procurement, maintenance and training brings costs down and delivery forward. The Tempest project, where the U.K., Italy and Japan are jointly building a next-generation fighter, demonstrates the model: shared development costs that no single country could carry alone. Recent bilateral maritime agreements, and Romania’s use of EU funding to buy European while expanding production at home, show the same logic spreading. The third is industrial consolidation, which is already underway and needs to move faster. Companies are driving it themselves. Airbus, Leonardo and Thales have agreed to merge their space divisions into a single joint venture with roughly €6.5 billion in revenue and 25,000 employees, and European defense mergers and acquisitions rose 35 percent year over year in the first half of 2025. McKinsey analysis finds that consolidation across key supply chain segments could unlock around €9 billion in annual synergies , more than the current equipment budgets of 24 of Europe’s 30 NATO members. The deepest opportunity sits below the big primes, among the thousands of tier two, three and four suppliers that still duplicate one another’s work. Europe can speed this up by harmonizing requirements, reducing national carve-outs and letting industry do the combining. Consolidation is only half the task. Europe also needs to build sheer capacity — more shipyards, more assembly lines, more of the physical plants that turn orders into hardware — and the capital to fund it. In several categories, Europe simply lacks enough places to build. Real deterrence means difficult choices, and a public that understands the importance and the cost of security. The fourth is regulatory unlocking. Full scale-up demands skilled workers retrained, accredited and security cleared from other industries; production sites with preapproved permitting; and alignment of export controls across European allies. These regulatory unlocks now need the same energy and focus as the funding commitment debate. Real deterrence means difficult choices, and a public that understands the importance and the cost of security. That conversation is only beginning in much of Europe. It must include the potential for “gray zone” cyber strikes on hospitals, arson at industrial sites, drones disrupting ports, undersea data cables cut — these have all occurred, but many citizens do not yet recognize this as having malicious intent. The opportunity in getting it right is significant. McKinsey and GLOBSEC estimates indicate that every euro of spending on European-manufactured equipment generates two euros of revenue across the European supply chain, and an additional €165 billion a year in equipment spending could create up to 1.2 million jobs . The coming years will reveal how effectively Europe is able to scale up to protect its territory and citizens, and how much of the promised investment becomes lasting deterrence and European jobs. Getting there depends on the whole ecosystem — governments, industry and investors — moving together. Increased spending is important. Spending it effectively matters more. https://telex.hu/transtelex/2026/08/21/s.text: Menü Kereső Gyergyóból is békülékeny üzenetet kapott a Tisza-kormány: „Minket a testvéri kapcsolat érdekel” Transtelex Bajkó Tibor és Ildikó főszervezők és Orosz László szervező között Kollai István, az új magyar kormány határon túli magyarokért felelős helyettes államtitkár – Fotó: Tőkés Hunor / Transtelex Tőkés Hunor (Transtelex) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Kolozsvár után Gyergyószentmiklóson folytatta első erdélyi látogatását Kollai István, az új magyar kormány határon túli magyarokért felelős helyettes államtitkára. A Székelyföldi Lovas Ünnepen a szervezők arra kérték, vigye Budapestre az üzenetet: Székelyföldön nem egy újabb magyar–magyar konfliktusban, hanem az együttműködésben érdekeltek. A több mint egy héten át tartó Kolozsvári Magyar Napokra érkezett Erdélybe Kollai István helyettes államtitkár , ám augusztus 20-át mégsem Kolozsváron töltötte. Egy székelyföldi meghívásnak tett eleget, és Gyergyószentmiklósra utazott, hogy részt vegyen az ott szervezett négynapos lovas ünnep nyitónapján, amelyen a szervezők azt üzenték: az erdélyi és magyarországi magyarok közötti összetartozást fontosabbnak tartják az aktuális politikai konfliktusoknál. A lovas rendezvény a Szent István-napi szekeres zarándoklattal kezdődött. Bajkó Tibor főszervező szerint 33 fogat és 8 lovas vett részt a zarándoklaton; a gyergyói és más székelyföldi résztvevők mellett még a dél-romániai Ialomița megyéből érkezett szekeresek is megjelentek, akiket tiszteletbeli székellyé kívánnak avatni. A Szent István-templomnál Kollai azt mondta, nem csak ünnepeken szeretnének jelen lenni Erdélyben. Szerinte „az ünnepnapok fejezik ki azt, hogy összetartozunk”, a hétköznapoknak pedig arról kellene szólniuk, hogy „nem csak összetartozunk, hanem összedolgozunk”. A helyettes államtitkár azt mondta, reméli, hogy a helyi vezetőkkel és a gyergyószentmiklósiakkal közösen tudnak terveket kitalálni és megvalósítani. Bajkó Tibor a helyettes államtitkárnak válaszolva fogalmazta meg, hogy azt üzenik Székelyföldről Magyarországra, hogy „minket a közösség, a testvéri kapcsolat érdekel. Mi nem rombolók akarunk lenni. Mi a nagy magyar nemzet tagjaiként egységes magyar szeretetben szeretnénk a Kárpát-medencében élni.” A főszervező hozzátette: ez azoknak a magyarországiaknak szól, akik „szeretik és elfogadják” a székelyeket. Kollai István néhány nappal korábban a Kolozsvári Magyar Napokon mutatkozott be hivatalosan az erdélyi közönség előtt . Ott az elmúlt tizenhat évben rendre a Fidesz-kormány képviselői kaptak helyet a megnyitón, idén viszont már az új magyar kormány helyettes államtitkára mondott beszédet. Kolozsváron Kollai maga is arról beszélt, hogy most pozitív üzenetekre, a kedélyek hűtésére és a magyarországi, illetve erdélyi magyarok közötti kölcsönös megértésre lenne szükség. Gyergyószentmiklósi jelenléte még a helyi politikai körök egy részét is meglepte. Politikai szereplők a háttérben egymást kérdezgették arról, hogy a helyettes államtitkár első székelyföldi útja miért éppen Gyergyóba vezetett. A találgatásokhoz hozzájárul, hogy az új magyar kormány éppen átvizsgálja a korábbi külhoni támogatási rendszert, Kollai pedig Kolozsváron azt mondta, 2027 elejéig szeretnék áttekinteni és kielemezni azt. Kollai István helyettes államtitkár a szekeres zarándoklaton – Fotók: Tőkés Hunor / Transtelex A Gyergyói-medence azért is érzékeny helyszín, mert az Orbán-kormány idején az erdélyi magyar állami gazdaságfejlesztés egyik leglátványosabb központjává vált . Gyergyóremetén Balázs Attila vállalkozásaihoz jelentős magyarországi támogatások kerültek, a Transtelex pedig nemrég részletesen bemutatta, hogy a magyarországi kormányváltás után több, az üzletemberhez kötődő projekt is megtorpant. A csütörtöki szekeres zarándoklat végállomásán, a Krigel pályán Kollai ismét beszédet mondott. Úgy fogalmazott, megható számára, hogy augusztus 20-át „magyar és székely zászlók közepette” ünnepelheti, és emlékeztetett arra is, hogy a budapesti parlamenten is ott van a székely zászló. Azt ígérte, lesznek még „fontos üzenetek a határon túlra”, és reményét fejezte ki, hogy minél többször visszatérhet. Azt is bejelentette, hogy Heidl György társadalmi kapcsolatokért felelős államtitkár szombaton szintén Erdélybe látogat. Ezután megkérdezte a jelenlévőket: „Egyetértünk, hogy összefogásban vagyunk érdekeltek?” A közönség helyesléssel és vastapssal reagált. Kollai később a legszebb szekeres fogatok díjainak átadásában is részt vett. Lovas ünnep a Kriegel lovaspályán – Fotók: Tőkés Hunor / Transtelex A rendezvény háttere közben pénzügyileg bizonytalan. A Transtelex a helyszínen megtudta, hogy idén a szervezés egy pontján az is felmerült: Bajkó Tibor nem rendezi meg a Lovas Ünnepet. A mindenki számára nyitott, ezért belépőjegy nélküli esemény köz- és magántámogatásokra épül, idén azonban a közintézményi források körül is volt bizonytalanság, miközben a nehezebb gazdasági helyzet miatt a vállalkozások is kevesebbet tudtak adni. Bajkó végül a megnyitón mintegy 160 támogatónak mondott köszönetet, és külön kiemelte a magyar kormányt, illetve a Bethlen Gábor Alapon keresztül érkező támogatást, amelyet a rendezvény színvonalának fenntartásához nélkülözhetetlennek nevezett. A Krigel Sport Klubot és lovas programjait a Bethlen Gábor Alap korábban is támogatta. A 2008-ban alapított Krigel Sport Klub által szervezett Székelyföldi Lovas Ünnep idén augusztus 20. és 23. között tart. A csütörtöki zarándoklat után pénteken lovas gyereknapot, díjugrató- és fogathajtóversenyeket rendeznek, hétvégén pedig munkalovas versenyek, lovaskaszkadőrök, lovasíjász-bemutató, szabadtéri szentmise és a polgármesterek hagyományos lovas vetélkedője is szerepel a programban.
